findings.description: With Blender Cloth self-collision enabled, direct inspection of all five views and six pose renders shows the overskirt expands into a dense mass of sharp, chaotic folds that projects far outside the hips and obscures its pleated silhouette. The side and three-quarter profiles show severe lateral ballooning; the crouch and sit retain thigh exposure and a long rear panel. Self-collision worsens the already rejected V172 appearance.

Irregular gray body-colored patches remain visible across the white chest and waist in neutral, arms-up, and arm-cross renders. The current evidence does not identify whether they are intersections, exposed source surfaces, or shading, so the cause remains unresolved.
In crouch and sit, both shorts-clad thighs still project in front of the overskirt while the center front panel falls behind them. Coverage and clearance remain unacceptable in bent-leg poses.

nextAction: Keep V173 rejected. Actual Blender 4.4.3 Cloth self-collision was enabled at self-distance 0.015 m; the bake worsened body clearance (409 negative signed-distance vertices after bake versus 416 before; V172 ended with zero), and the attached 710-vertex hem band moved 0.3415 m maximum / 0.2237 m mean (V172: 0.2628 m / 0.0922 m). Do not try another bending-stiffness or self-collision setting. Replace the current dense native-cloth skirt bake with a geometry/attachment method that preserves the authored sewn-panel silhouette and keeps the hem bound to its source edges; measure panel deformation, signed body clearance, and bent-leg coverage before changing the bodice. After that correction, regenerate and directly inspect all eleven current renders. Fit, Shape Key response, Unity/VRChat execution, packaging, and release remain unverified.
